# Richard Sykes — LinkedIn Profile Rework

## Purpose of this document

This is a working LinkedIn profile source document. It is not intended to be uploaded directly as-is.

Use it as a controlled profile pack containing:

- Preferred headline
- Alternative headline options
- About section
- Experience section copy
- Featured section recommendations
- Skills and keyword strategy
- Open to Work recruiter settings
- Ongoing update notes

The LinkedIn profile should act as the front-end advert in the wider sales pipeline:

> LinkedIn creates interest. GitHub proves the technical substance. The CV closes the conversation.

---

# 1. Strategic Positioning

## Target Position

**Hands-on technology leader for quantitative risk, model platforms and regulated analytical systems.**

## Core Message

> I build trusted, cloud-native platforms for complex quantitative decision-making.

## Expanded Message

> I help regulated, data-heavy organisations turn complex models, data workflows and governance requirements into scalable, auditable platforms that people can trust.

## What LinkedIn Must Communicate Quickly

The profile should make the reader understand that Richard is:

- Senior enough to lead platform direction
- Technical enough to still build, review and challenge architecture
- Domain-aware enough to work in regulated financial services
- Commercial enough to understand business-critical delivery
- Distinctive enough to stand out from generic engineering managers, cloud architects or credit risk modellers

## What LinkedIn Should Avoid

The profile should avoid over-positioning Richard as:

- A narrow credit risk modeller
- A generic Azure engineer
- A detached people manager
- A pure quant researcher
- A fintech enthusiast without serious delivery evidence

---

# 2. Recommended LinkedIn Headline

## Preferred Headline

**Hands-on Technology Leader | Quantitative Risk Platforms | Azure, Python, Model Governance & Regulated Systems**

## Why this works

This headline leads with senior identity, keeps the technical credibility, and broadens the role beyond credit risk model implementation.

It also gives LinkedIn enough keyword coverage across:

- Technology leadership
- Quantitative risk
- Platform architecture
- Azure
- Python
- Model governance
- Regulated systems

---

# 3. Alternative Headline Options

## Option A — Most Executive

**Technology Leader for Regulated Quantitative Platforms | Risk, Model Governance, Azure & Python Engineering**

Best for: Director, Head-of, CTO-track positioning.

## Option B — Most Technical

**Principal / Lead Engineer | Quantitative Risk Platforms | Python, Azure, APIs, SDKs & Cloud-Native Architecture**

Best for: Principal Engineer, Staff Engineer, Platform Architect roles.

## Option C — Most Recruiter-Friendly

**Lead Quantitative Developer | Credit Risk Platforms | Azure, Python, IFRS 9, IRB, Model Governance**

Best for: matching known financial services recruiter searches.

## Option D — Strong Current-State Version

**Lead Quantitative Developer at Investec | Platform Architecture, Credit Risk Models, Azure & Python**

Best for: conservative update if avoiding a major repositioning.

## Option E — High-Impact Version

**Hands-on Technology Leader | Building Trusted Platforms for Quantitative Risk, Analytics & Model Governance**

Best for: personal brand clarity, less keyword dense.

---

# 4. Recommended About Section

## Version 1 — Preferred Balanced Version

I am a hands-on technology leader specialising in cloud-native platforms for quantitative, regulated and analytical decision systems.

My work sits where models, data, engineering and governance meet. I lead the implementation of credit risk models and the platforms around them: model execution, monitoring, impact assessment, data lineage, evidence tracking, self-service tooling and executive reporting.

I started my career in automotive engineering, emissions modelling and optimisation, working with complex physical systems, time-series data, simulation and predictive models. That background still shapes how I think: understand the system, measure it properly, remove friction, automate repeatable work, and build tools that make better decisions easier.

At Investec, I lead platform delivery for credit risk model implementation across IFRS 9 and IRB frameworks. My work spans Python, Azure, FastAPI, Pydantic, SQL, CI/CD, TDD, observability and cloud-native architecture. The goal is not technology for its own sake. The goal is trusted decision infrastructure: systems that are scalable, auditable and useful to the people who rely on them.

I still stay close to the tools. I build, review, prototype and shape technical standards directly, while also leading people, delivery and cross-functional alignment across Risk, quantitative teams, technology, audit and senior stakeholders.

Alongside my professional work, I continue to develop personal engineering projects around systematic allocation, macro signals, portfolio risk and explainable decision workflows. I am also actively extending my technical depth through Azure, AI, data and architecture certifications.

My direction is towards broader technology leadership across risk platforms, model infrastructure, regulated analytics and AI-enabled decision systems.

# 5. Alternative About Section Versions

## Version 2 — Shorter Recruiter Version

Hands-on technology leader and quantitative developer with 15+ years’ experience building production systems across regulated financial services and automotive engineering.

I currently lead credit risk model platform delivery at Investec, working across IFRS 9, IRB, model governance, impact assessment, monitoring and cloud-native infrastructure. My focus is turning complex quantitative and regulatory requirements into scalable, auditable platforms that support better business decisions.

My technical background spans Python, Azure, FastAPI, Pydantic, SQL, CI/CD, TDD, data pipelines and model execution frameworks. I still stay close to the tools: building reference implementations, shaping SDKs and APIs, reviewing architecture, improving developer experience and applying engineering discipline in high-control environments.

Earlier in my career, I worked in automotive powertrain and emissions optimisation at Prodrive and Ford, building predictive models, automation tooling and analytical platforms for complex engineering datasets. That systems-optimisation mindset still underpins how I approach risk technology today.

I am interested in senior roles across risk technology, quantitative platforms, model infrastructure, regulated analytics, cloud-native engineering and AI-enabled decision systems.

## Version 3 — More Executive Version

I build trusted platforms for complex quantitative decision-making.

My career has moved from automotive optimisation and emissions modelling into financial services technology, where I now lead cloud-native platform delivery for credit risk model implementation in a regulated banking environment.

The common thread is systems thinking: complex data, complex models, high-stakes decisions, and the need for repeatable, explainable, well-governed engineering.

At Investec, my work spans credit risk model execution, monitoring, impact assessment, governance workflows, Python SDKs, Azure infrastructure, CI/CD, test-driven delivery and stakeholder-facing tooling. I work closely with quantitative teams, Risk, technology, audit and senior stakeholders to turn model and regulatory complexity into platforms that scale.

I am a hands-on leader. I still build and review code, shape architecture, define engineering standards and prototype new patterns, while also leading delivery and developing people.

My next chapter is focused on broader technology leadership across regulated analytics, risk platforms, model governance, AI-assisted engineering and decision infrastructure.

# 6. Experience Section — Investec

## Current Role Title

**Lead Quantitative Developer — Credit Risk Model Platforms**

## Company

Investec

## Date

July 2017 – Present

## Recommended Description

Lead platform delivery for credit risk model implementation across IFRS 9 and IRB frameworks, working at the intersection of quantitative modelling, software engineering, cloud infrastructure, risk governance and business-critical decision-making.

Responsible for translating complex regulatory and model requirements into scalable, auditable platform capabilities used by Credit, Risk, quantitative teams and business stakeholders.

Key areas of ownership:

- Credit risk model execution and implementation
- Model monitoring and lifecycle tooling
- Impact assessment infrastructure
- Self-service model output interrogation
- Python SDK and API design
- Azure cloud-native architecture
- CI/CD, TDD and controlled delivery practices
- Data lineage, evidence tracking and audit support
- Cross-functional delivery across Risk, technology, quantitative teams and audit stakeholders

Selected achievements:

- Led delivery of cloud-native credit risk platform capabilities across IFRS 9 and IRB model frameworks.
- Built self-service tooling enabling business and risk users to interrogate model outputs and drivers without creating bottlenecks in the modelling team.
- Designed hierarchical Python SDK and abstraction patterns to standardise model development workflows across multiple teams.
- Increased critical model testing throughput from 2–3 runs per day to 8 runs per day by removing infrastructure and workflow bottlenecks.
- Supported Big Four audit reviews with no findings within owned implementation and control scope.
- Delivered high-net-worth mortgage affordability calculation capability under FCA MCOB 11.6 requirements.
- Introduced governed AI-assisted engineering patterns, including structured context, reusable prompts/workflows and AI-assisted code review approaches.
- Managed and developed team members through high-pressure regulatory delivery cycles.

Technical environment:

Python, FastAPI, Pydantic, SQLAlchemy, SQL, Azure Container Apps, Azure Functions, Azure SQL, Cosmos DB, Azure Machine Learning, Azure DevOps, Docker, Application Insights, PyTest, TDD, CI/CD, Bicep.

## Date

February 2014 – July 2017

Led predictive analytics and automation work across automotive engineering datasets, supporting emissions, CO₂, NVH and powertrain optimisation activities within a multinational OEM environment.

Key areas of ownership:

- Predictive modelling and time-series analysis
- SQL and Python automation tooling
- Engineering data pipelines
- Analytical reporting and visualisation
- Team leadership and roadmap ownership
- Source control adoption and development discipline

Selected achievements:

- Led a team of seven analysts and acted as local SME for novel analytical requests.
- Automated a significant proportion of recurring analytical workload using SQL and Python tooling, reducing manual effort and specialist dependency.
- Built data-processing workflows for heterogeneous engineering datasets including vehicle, dyno, emissions and calibration data.
- Supported large-scale predictive modelling across CO₂, emissions and NVH workflows.
- Introduced GitHub source control and improved development discipline across collaborative MATLAB projects.
- Worked with product development, advanced research and engineering stakeholders across a multinational OEM.

Technical environment:

Python, MATLAB, SQL Server, Pandas, NumPy, neural networks, time-series analysis, automation scripts, data visualisation, Excel/PowerPoint automation.

# 9. Featured Section Strategy

The Featured section should act as the shop window for the sales pipeline.

## Recommended Featured Items

1. **GitHub Profile**  
   Purpose: show hands-on technical credibility and public engineering portfolio.

2. **Atlas Allocation Repository**  
   Purpose: show personal technical curiosity, systematic investing, macro/factor/risk thinking and layered platform design.

3. **CV Repository or PDF Link**  
   Purpose: give interested recruiters and hiring managers the sales brochure.

4. **Selected Certification / Microsoft Learn Profile**  
   Purpose: show active technical development across Azure, AI and data.

5. **Optional Thought Leadership Post**  
   Example topic: “Why model governance needs platform engineering, not spreadsheets.”

# 12. Profile URL / Contact Strategy

## Public Links

The profile should clearly link to:

- GitHub homepage
- CV or CV repository
- Atlas Allocation project, if public
- Microsoft Learn / certification profile, if presentable

## Contact Tone

Avoid sounding too eager. Use confident availability language.

Recommended:

> Open to senior technical leadership conversations across risk platforms, regulated analytics, model infrastructure and cloud-native engineering.

Avoid:

> Actively looking for new opportunities.

---

# 13. Content / Posting Strategy

LinkedIn will work better if the profile is supported by occasional thoughtful posts.

## Recommended Post Themes

1. **Model platforms**  
   Why model governance needs engineering platforms, not just documentation.

2. **AI-assisted engineering**  
   How to use AI coding tools in regulated environments without losing control.

3. **Python SDK design**  
   Why internal platforms need good developer experience.

4. **Risk technology**  
   The gap between model development and production implementation.

5. **Automotive to finance career arc**  
   What emissions optimisation taught me about financial risk systems.

6. **Atlas Allocation**  
   Building a systematic macro/factor/risk framework as a personal engineering project.

## Posting Cadence

A realistic cadence is one strong post every 4–6 weeks.

Quality matters more than frequency.

---

# 14. Phrases to Use

Use these phrases naturally across the profile:

- Trusted decision infrastructure
- Regulated analytical systems
- Quantitative risk platforms
- Cloud-native model infrastructure
- Model execution and governance
- Platform abstractions
- Developer experience
- Audit-grade delivery
- Systems thinking
- Hands-on technical leadership
- Explainable workflows
- Business-critical models
- Controlled AI-assisted engineering

---

# 15. Phrases to Avoid

Avoid or minimise:

- Passionate about fintech
- Highly skilled
- Can-do attitude
- Guru / expert in everything
- Responsible for
- Worked on
- Involved in
- Rock star / ninja language
- Generic transformation language
- Overly broad “AI leader” claims

---

# 16. Recommended Profile Summary for Recruiter Conversations

Use this when speaking to recruiters or writing short intros.

> I am a hands-on technology leader currently leading credit risk model platform delivery at Investec. My background spans automotive optimisation, predictive modelling and regulated financial services technology. I specialise in cloud-native platforms for model execution, governance, monitoring and analytical decision workflows, mainly across Python, Azure, APIs, SDKs, SQL, CI/CD and TDD. I am interested in senior roles across risk technology, quantitative platforms, regulated analytics and model infrastructure where I can stay technically close while increasing platform and leadership scope.

---

# 17. Final LinkedIn Acceptance Criteria

The LinkedIn profile is successful if:

- A recruiter can understand the market category within 10 seconds.
- A CTO or Head of Engineering sees senior technical leadership potential.
- A risk leader sees domain credibility.
- A senior engineer sees enough technical substance to respect the profile.
- The profile encourages the reader to click GitHub or request the CV.
- The profile does not trap Richard as only a credit risk modeller.
- The profile communicates ambition without sounding inflated.

---
